blocks.html:
READING PASSAGE 3

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 27–40, which are based on Reading Passage 3 below.

Some views on the use of headphones

Whether wearing headphones at work, or in other areas of everyday life, is a good thing or a bad thing has generated a lot of research and opinion

To visit a typical modern office today is to walk into a room with possibly a dozen songs playing simultaneously but to hear none of them. Up to half of younger workers listen to music on their headphones, and nearly all of them think it makes them better at their jobs. In survey after survey, people report with confidence that music makes them happier, better at concentrating, and more productive.

Scientists do not share this belief; they maintain that listening to music hurts people's ability to recall other things they should be doing, and any pop song, loud or soft, reduces overall performance for both extroverts and introverts. A Taiwanese study linked music that has lyrics to lower marks on concentration tests for college students, and other research has shown music with lyrics scrambles our brains' verbal-processing skills. “As silence has the best overall performance, it would still be advisable that people work in silence,” another reporter dryly concluded.

The question is therefore: if headphones are so bad for productivity, why do so many people at work have them? One factor to consider is that countries like the USA have moved from a farming and manufacturing economy to a service economy, with an emphasis on jobs in offices that require higher levels of concentration, reflection and creativity. As an estimated 70 percent of office workers work in open-plan office spaces, it is more important to create one's own enclosing bubble of sound. Lending strength to the argument for headphones at work is evidence that music relaxes our muscles, improves our mood, and may even moderately reduce blood pressure, heart rate and anxiety.

The story of headphones began in 1910, when the US Navy received an odd letter written in purple ink on blue-and-pink paper. The letter writer, an eccentric inventor and repairman named Nathaniel Baldwin, from the US state of Utah, made what at the time was an astonishing claim: he had built, in his kitchen, a new kind of headset that could amplify sound. This was an opportune invention for the Navy, which asked for a sound test and then enthusiastically adopted the headsets, later called headphones, and used them in World War I for naval radio communication.

The purpose of headphones is to concentrate a quiet and private sound in the ear of the listener, which is a radical departure from music's social purpose in history. “Music, together with dance, co-evolved biologically and culturally to serve as a technology of social bonding,” Nils L. Wallin and Björn Merker wrote in The Origins of Music. Songs don't leave behind bones, but evidence of musical notation dates back to Sumeria, 3,500 years ago, and in 1995 archaeologists discovered a bone flute in southern Europe estimated to be 44,000 years old. If music evolved as a social glue for the species, as a way to make groups and keep them together, headphones have done what writing and literacy did for language - they made music private.

Author and columnist Stephen Marche wrote that separation from other people is one of the first things ordinary Americans spend their money achieving. It is “a by-product of a long-standing national appetite for independence,” he said. Americans are not alone in their desire for personal independence and privacy. Marche is right; wealth can buy – and modern technology can deliver – personal independence, and it is this that people have always sought.

Dr Michael Bull, an expert on personal music devices from the University of Sussex in the UK, has repeatedly made the larger point that personal music devices change how we relate to public spaces. Controlling our public spaces is more important now that more people are moving from the edges of cities to live in urban centres. "With the urban space, the more it's inhabited, the safer you feel,” Bull says. “You feel safe if you can feel people there, but you don't want to interact with them.” Headphones create shields for wearers, separating them from other people and their surroundings. Headphones have their own rules of good manners; they are like wearing a “Do not disturb” sign. We assume that people wearing them are busy and we should respect their privacy, so now people wear them to appear busy. In fact, it is now becoming quite common for people not to listen to anything at all, but just to wear headphones.

However, as pointed out at the beginning of this piece, although scientists have stated that headphones are bad for productivity, people still wear them at work. It is not just that headphones create privacy out of public areas, but also that music causes people to relax and reflect and pause. The outcome of relaxation, reflection and pausing at work won't be captured in minute-to-minute productivity metrics. What must be considered is that in moments of extreme focus, our attention radiates outward, toward the problem, rather than inward, on how to solve the problem. However, with music “When our minds are at ease, we're more likely to direct the spotlight of attention inward,” Jonah Lehrer wrote in his book Imagine: How Creativity Works. “The answers have been there all along. We just weren't listening." In a crowded world, real estate is the ultimate scarce resource, and a headphone is a small invisible fence around our minds – making space, creating separation, and helping us listen to ourselves.

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 1
passageNotes.text: 如今走进典型现代办公室，常能看到近半数年轻员工戴耳机听音乐，且几乎所有人都认为这能提升工作表现 —— 调查显示，人们坚信音乐能让人更快乐、专注且高效。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 2
passageNotes.text: 但科学家持相反观点：听音乐会损害记忆力，无论外向者还是内向者，任何流行音乐（无论音量）都会降低整体表现。台湾研究发现带歌词的音乐会降低大学生专注力测试分数，其他研究也表明歌词会干扰大脑语言处理能力。有研究者直言 “安静环境下表现最佳，工作时应保持安静”。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 3
passageNotes.text: 核心疑问是 “若耳机对效率有害，为何职场中如此普遍？” 原因之一是美国等国家从农业制造业经济转向服务业，办公室工作需更高专注力、思考与创造力；约 70% 办公室员工在开放式空间工作，耳机能帮助构建 “个人声音气泡”。此外，有证据表明音乐能放松肌肉、改善情绪，甚至轻微降低血压、心率与焦虑，为职场使用耳机提供支持。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 4
passageNotes.text: 耳机的起源可追溯至 1910 年 —— 美国犹他州古怪发明家兼修理工纳撒尼尔・鲍德温（Nathaniel Baldwin）用紫色墨水在粉蓝纸上写信给美国海军，声称在厨房发明了 “能放大声音的新型头戴设备”。海军测试后积极采用，将其用于一战海军无线电通信，“耳机（headphones）” 由此诞生。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 5
passageNotes.text: 耳机的核心功能是 “将安静私密的声音集中传入听者耳朵”，这彻底改变了音乐的历史社交属性。正如《音乐的起源》中所言 “音乐与舞蹈共同进化，作为社会联结的工具”—— 音乐的历史可追溯至 3500 年前的苏美尔乐谱，甚至 4.4 万年前的骨笛。若音乐是 “社会黏合剂”，耳机则像文字对语言的作用 —— 让音乐从公共变为私人。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 6
passageNotes.text: 作家兼专栏作家斯蒂芬・马什（Stephen Marche）指出，“与他人保持距离” 是美国人愿意花钱实现的目标，这是 “长期追求独立的副产品”。不仅美国人，全球人都渴望个人独立与隐私 —— 财富与现代技术能实现这种独立，这是人类的普遍追求。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 7
passageNotes.text: 英国萨塞克斯大学的迈克尔・布尔（Michael Bull）博士强调，个人音乐设备改变了人类与公共空间的关系。如今更多人从郊区迁往市中心，控制公共空间体验愈发重要 ——“城市空间居住者越多越安全，但人们不愿互动”。耳机为使用者构建 “屏障”，像 “请勿打扰” 标识，甚至有人戴耳机仅为 “显得忙碌”，实际并未播放音乐。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 8
passageNotes.text: 尽管科学家认为耳机损害效率，人们仍在工作中使用 —— 耳机不仅创造私人空间，还能让人放松、反思与暂停。这种放松的效果无法用 “分钟级效率指标” 衡量：高度专注时，注意力向外聚焦于问题；而音乐让大脑放松，注意力向内聚焦于解决方案（乔纳森・莱勒在《想象：创造力如何运作》中指出 “放松时更易找到答案”）。在拥挤世界中，耳机是 “思维周围的隐形小栅栏”—— 创造空间、保持距离，帮助人们倾听内心。

items.text:
（1）题目 27：Young people are easily persuaded by surveys that listening to music is beneficial.（年轻人易被调查说服，认为听音乐有益）
答案：NOT GIVEN（未提及）
解析：定位 Paragraph 1 中 “Up to half of younger workers listen to music on their headphones, and nearly all of them think it makes them better at their jobs. In survey after survey, people report with confidence that music makes them happier...”，仅提到 “年轻人自信报告音乐好处”，未提及 “被调查说服”，无相关信息，因此判定为 NOT GIVEN。

（2）题目 28：Different studies share the same conclusions about the desirability of working in silence.（不同研究对 “安静工作有益” 的结论一致）
答案：YES（正确）
解析：定位 Paragraph 2 中 “Scientists do not share this belief; they maintain that listening to music hurts... A Taiwanese study linked music that has lyrics to lower marks... other research has shown music with lyrics scrambles... ‘As silence has the best overall performance, it would still be advisable that people work in silence’”，不同研究均得出 “安静工作表现最佳” 的结论，与题干描述一致，因此判定为 YES。

（3）题目 29：Some doctors recommend wearing headphones to lower blood pressure.（部分医生建议戴耳机以降低血压）
答案：NOT GIVEN（未提及）
解析：定位 Paragraph 3 中 “music relaxes our muscles, improves our mood, and may even moderately reduce blood pressure”，仅提到 “音乐可能降低血压”，未提及 “医生建议戴耳机”，无相关信息，因此判定为 NOT GIVEN。

（4）题目 30：Nathaniel Baldwin was a respected government researcher.（纳撒尼尔・鲍德温是受尊重的政府研究员）
答案：NO（错误）
解析：定位 Paragraph 4 中 “an eccentric inventor and repairman named Nathaniel Baldwin”，“古怪的发明家兼修理工” 与题干 “受尊重的政府研究员” 描述矛盾，因此判定为 NO。

（5）题目 31：The effect of the invention of headphones is comparable to the effect of the invention of writing.（耳机发明的影响可与文字发明的影响相比）
答案：YES（正确）
解析：定位 Paragraph 5 中 “headphones have done what writing and literacy did for language – they made music private”，“耳机让音乐私人化，正如文字对语言的作用”，明确将两者影响类比，与题干描述一致，因此判定为 YES。

items.text:
（1）题目 32：What does the writer suggest about a service economy?（作者关于服务经济有何暗示？）
答案：A（The work is mentally demanding. 工作对脑力要求高）
解析：定位 Paragraph 3 中 “countries like the USA have moved from a farming and manufacturing economy to a service economy, with an emphasis on jobs in offices that require higher levels of concentration, reflection and creativity”，“更高专注力、思考与创造力” 对应 “mentally demanding”，因此选 A。B（为年轻人提供就业）、C（占经济体比例小）、D（员工需住在市中心）均未提及。

（2）题目 33：When the writer mentions the historical evidence for early music, he is（作者提及早期音乐的历史证据，目的是？）
答案：C（lending support to the view that music has been important in human history. 支持 “音乐在人类历史中一直重要” 的观点）
解析：定位 Paragraph 5 中 “evidence of musical notation dates back to Sumeria, 3,500 years ago, and in 1995 archaeologists discovered a bone flute in southern Europe estimated to be 44,000 years old. If music evolved as a social glue for the species”，通过苏美尔乐谱与骨笛的例子，证明 “音乐长期作为社会黏合剂”，即 “历史中一直重要”，因此选 C。A（强调音乐形式多样性）、B（表达对考古证据有限的沮丧）、D（绘制音乐进化地理图）均偏离目的。

（3）题目 34：What does the writer say about the social effects of listening to music through headphones?（作者关于戴耳机听音乐的社会影响有何观点？）
答案：D（It has changed the traditional role of music in society. 改变了音乐在社会中的传统角色）
解析：定位 Paragraph 5 中 “The purpose of headphones is to concentrate a quiet and private sound in the ear of the listener, which is a radical departure from music’s social purpose in history... headphones have done what writing and literacy did for language – they made music private”，“从社会功能转为私人功能” 对应 “changed the traditional role”，因此选 D。A（减少听音乐的人数）、B（增加音乐活动参与度）、C（减少音乐风格的全球多样性）均未提及。

（4）题目 35：What does the writer say about personal independence?（作者关于个人独立有何观点？）
答案：B（Personal independence is something that can be purchased. 个人独立是可购买的事物）
解析：定位 Paragraph 6 中 “wealth can buy – and modern technology can deliver – personal independence”，“财富可购买独立” 对应 “can be purchased”，因此选 B。A（美国人对独立的渴望独特）、C（追求独立是近期现象）、D（独立破坏社会联结）均与原文矛盾或未提及。

（5）题目 36：Why does the writer quote Jonah Lehrer in the last paragraph?（作者在最后一段引用乔纳森・莱勒的话，目的是？）
答案：A（To support the writer’s own view. 支持作者自身观点）
解析：定位 Paragraph 8 中 “with music ‘When our minds are at ease, we’re more likely to direct the spotlight of attention inward,’ Jonah Lehrer wrote... ‘The answers have been there all along. We just weren’t listening.’ In a crowded world... a headphone is a small invisible fence around our minds – making space, creating separation, and helping us listen to ourselves”，引用莱勒 “放松时更易找到答案” 的观点，支撑作者 “耳机帮助人们反思、倾听内心” 的观点，因此选 A。B（吸引对权威书籍的关注）、C（提高对倾听能力丧失的重视）、D（说明音乐拉近人与人距离）均偏离目的。

items.text:
（1）题目 37：Dr Michael Bull believes that listening to music through headphones has changed the \___\___ the wearers of headphones have with public spaces.（迈克尔・布尔博士认为，戴耳机听音乐改变了使用者与公共空间的_\___\__。）
答案：B（relationship，关系）
解析：定位 Paragraph 7 中 “Dr Michael Bull... has repeatedly made the larger point that personal music devices change how we relate to public spaces”，“how we relate to”（如何与…… 关联）对应 “relationship”，因此选 B。

（2）题目 38：Living in the centre of cities is becoming popular, as people become less keen on living in the \___\___.（住在市中心愈发流行，因人们对住在_\___\__的兴趣降低。）
答案：E（suburbs，郊区）
解析：定位 Paragraph 7 中 “more people are moving from the edges of cities to live in urban centres”，“从城市边缘（郊区）迁往市中心” 对应 “less keen on living in the suburbs”，因此选 E。

（3）题目 39：In densely populated city centres, headphones form \___\___ that isolate people from fellow citizens and from their environment.（在人口密集的市中心，耳机构成_\___\__，将人们与他人及环境隔离。）
答案：G（barriers，屏障）
解析：定位 Paragraph 7 中 “Headphones create shields for wearers, separating them from other people and their surroundings”，“shields（护盾）” 对应 “barriers（屏障）”，因此选 G。

（4）题目 40：Wearers of headphones are treated with \___\___ that other people do not receive.（戴耳机的人会得到其他人得不到的_\___\__。）
答案：A（courtesy，礼貌）
解析：定位 Paragraph 7 中 “We assume that people wearing them are busy and we should respect their privacy”，“尊重隐私” 对应 “treated with courtesy（被礼貌对待）”，因此选 A。

questionExplanations.text:
答案：B（relationship，关系）
